Every week, one map per protected area with the new alerts: this is the kind of task that **should not
be done by hand**. With 7 protected areas that is already 7 maps; with 130, nobody keeps up.

The scripts I used did this in **ArcMap**, with `arcpy.mapping`: they opened an `.mxd`, changed the layer
filter, zoomed to the protected area and exported a JPEG. That module **does not exist in ArcGIS Pro**.
Here is the same idea in each program, from the old script to the license-free version.

![Map generated by the QGIS Atlas for Jamanxim National Park (labels in Portuguese). The same layout was exported for the 7 protected areas of the study area.](../imagens/artigos/mapa_atlas.png){fig-alt="Landscape A4 map titled Parque Nacional do Jamanxim. The protected area is shown in green with a thick black outline, the 3 km surrounding band in yellow, neighboring protected areas in light grey and DETER alerts colored by class. On the right, a legend, a 0 to 40 km scale bar, a north arrow and the data source."}

## What every automated map needs

1. A **template** (layout) with map, title, legend, scale bar, north arrow and source.
2. A **layer that drives the series** (the protected areas): each feature becomes a page.
3. **Title and filters that change** with the page (the protected area's name, only its surroundings).
4. **Automatic zoom** to the page's feature, with a margin.
5. **Export** with one file name per protected area (the CNUC code is better than the name, which has
   accents and spaces).

| | Template | Series | Changing text |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArcMap | `.mxd` | Python loop with `arcpy.mapping` | `ListLayoutElements("TEXT_ELEMENT")` |
| ArcGIS Pro | layout in the `.aprx` | **Map Series** | dynamic text `<dyn type="page" property="name"/>` |
| QGIS | print layout | **Atlas** | expression `[% "nome_uc" %]` |
| Python | matplotlib figure | `for` loop | f-string |

## The code

Names in Portuguese: `mapa` = map, `titulo` = title, `legenda` = legend, `escala` = scale bar,
`norte` = north arrow, `fonte` = source, `quadro` = map frame, `colocar` = place, `regras` = rules.

::: {.panel-tabset group="programa"}

## ArcMap

The old script, simplified. Runs only in **ArcMap 10.x** (Python 2.7).

```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import arcpy

mxd = arcpy.mapping.MapDocument(r"C:\dados\mapa_uc.mxd")
df = arcpy.mapping.ListDataFrames(mxd, "Layers")[0]
ucs = arcpy.mapping.ListLayers(mxd, "UCs", df)[0]
titulo = arcpy.mapping.ListLayoutElements(mxd, "TEXT_ELEMENT", "titulo")[0]

for cnuc, nome in arcpy.da.SearchCursor(ucs, ["cnuc", "nome_uc"]):
    ucs.definitionQuery = "cnuc = '%s'" % cnuc
    df.extent = ucs.getExtent()
    df.scale = df.scale * 1.1                      # 10% margin
    titulo.text = nome
    arcpy.mapping.ExportToPNG(mxd, r"C:\dados\mapas\mapa_%s.png" % cnuc, resolution=150)
    print "Map of %s exported" % nome
ucs.definitionQuery = ""
del mxd
```

To bring this layout into ArcGIS Pro, open a project and use **Insert → Import Map** with the `.mxd`.

## ArcGIS Pro

**Without code:** in the layout, **Layout → Map Series → Spatial**, index layer = protected areas, name
field = `nome_uc`. In the title, insert **Dynamic Text → Map Series → Page Name**. Then
**Share → Export Layout** and choose "All pages" and "One file per page".

**With code** (`arcpy.mp`), for full control of each step:

```python
import arcpy

projeto = arcpy.mp.ArcGISProject(r"C:\dados\mapas.aprx")
layout = projeto.listLayouts("Mapa por UC")[0]
quadro = layout.listElements("MAPFRAME_ELEMENT")[0]
titulo = layout.listElements("TEXT_ELEMENT", "titulo")[0]
ucs = quadro.map.listLayers("UCs")[0]

for cnuc, nome in arcpy.da.SearchCursor(ucs, ["cnuc", "nome_uc"]):
    ucs.definitionQuery = f"cnuc = '{cnuc}'"
    quadro.camera.setExtent(quadro.getLayerExtent(ucs, False, True))
    quadro.camera.scale *= 1.1                     # 10% margin
    titulo.text = nome
    layout.exportToPNG(rf"C:\dados\mapas\mapa_{cnuc}.png", resolution=150)
    print(f"Map of {nome} exported")
ucs.definitionQuery = ""
```

If the layout already has a map series set up, exporting takes one line:

```python
layout.mapSeries.exportToPDF(r"C:\dados\mapas\mapas.pdf", "ALL", multiple_files="PDF_SINGLE_FILE")
```

## QGIS

**Without code:** in the print layout, **Atlas → Generate an atlas** tab, coverage layer = protected
areas, file name = `'mapa_' || "cnuc"`. On the map item, check **Controlled by atlas** with a 10%
margin. In the title, use **Insert expression** with `[% "nome_uc" %]`. Export with
**Atlas → Export atlas as images**.

**With code** (Python console), the whole layout built from scratch, to run on any computer:

```python
import os
from qgis.core import (QgsProject, QgsVectorLayer, QgsPrintLayout, QgsLayoutItemMap,
                       QgsLayoutItemLabel, QgsLayoutItemLegend, QgsLayoutItemScaleBar,
                       QgsLayoutItemPicture, QgsLayoutPoint, QgsLayoutSize, QgsUnitTypes,
                       QgsLayoutExporter, QgsCategorizedSymbolRenderer, QgsRendererCategory,
                       QgsFillSymbol, QgsSingleSymbolRenderer, QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem,
                       QgsCoordinateTransform, QgsRuleBasedRenderer)
from qgis.PyQt.QtGui import QFont

G = "C:/dados/artigos.gpkg"
PASTA = "C:/dados/mapas/"
os.makedirs(PASTA, exist_ok=True)
projeto = QgsProject.instance()
MM = QgsUnitTypes.LayoutMillimeters

def poligono(**estilo):
    return QgsFillSymbol.createSimple(estilo)

# 1. Layers and styles: protected areas (they drive the atlas), surroundings and alerts since Aug 2026
ucs = QgsVectorLayer(f"{G}|layername=ucs", "Protected area", "ogr")
ucs.setSubsetString("regiao = 'Amazonia'")
extensao_ucs = ucs.extent()
def regras(*lista):
    """Rule-based style: (label, expression, symbol). @atlas_feature is the page's protected area."""
    raiz = QgsRuleBasedRenderer.Rule(None)
    for rotulo, expressao, simbolo in lista:
        raiz.appendChild(QgsRuleBasedRenderer.Rule(simbolo, filterExp=expressao, label=rotulo))
    return QgsRuleBasedRenderer(raiz)

ucs.setRenderer(regras(
    ("Mapped protected area", "@atlas_featureid = $id",
     poligono(color="229,236,220", outline_color="0,0,0", outline_width="0.8")),
    ("Other protected areas", "@atlas_featureid <> $id",
     poligono(color="242,242,242", outline_color="150,150,150", outline_width="0.3"))))
entorno = QgsVectorLayer(f"{G}|layername=ucs_entorno", "Surroundings", "ogr")
entorno.setRenderer(regras(
    ("3 km surroundings", "\"cnuc\" = attribute(@atlas_feature, 'cnuc')",
     poligono(color="240,228,66,140", outline_style="no"))))
alertas = QgsVectorLayer(f"{G}|layername=deter", "DETER alerts", "ogr")
alertas.setSubsetString("view_date >= '2026-08-01'")
classes = [("DESMATAMENTO_CR", "213,94,0", "Deforestation (clear-cut)"),
           ("MINERACAO", "204,121,167", "Mining"),
           ("DEGRADACAO", "230,159,0", "Degradation"),
           ("CICATRIZ_DE_QUEIMADA", "86,180,233", "Burn scar")]
categorias = [QgsRendererCategory(valor, poligono(color=cor, outline_color=cor,
                                                  outline_width="0.15"), rotulo)
              for valor, cor, rotulo in classes]
categorias.append(QgsRendererCategory(None, poligono(color="120,120,120", outline_style="no"),
                                      "Other classes"))
alertas.setRenderer(QgsCategorizedSymbolRenderer("classname", categorias))
projeto.addMapLayers([ucs, entorno, alertas])

# 2. Landscape A4 layout (each item is added and then placed, in millimeters)
layout = QgsPrintLayout(projeto)
layout.initializeDefaults()

def colocar(item, x, y, largura=None, altura=None):
    layout.addLayoutItem(item)
    item.attemptMove(QgsLayoutPoint(x, y, MM))
    if largura:
        item.attemptResize(QgsLayoutSize(largura, altura, MM))
    return item

mapa = QgsLayoutItemMap(layout)
crs_mapa = QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem("EPSG:5880")       # in meters: correct scale
mapa.setCrs(crs_mapa)
mapa.setLayers([alertas, entorno, ucs])
mapa.setFrameEnabled(True)
colocar(mapa, 8, 22, 200, 180)
# Initial extent: without it, the atlas stretches the map frame on the first page
para_metros = QgsCoordinateTransform(ucs.crs(), crs_mapa, projeto)
mapa.zoomToExtent(para_metros.transformBoundingBox(extensao_ucs))

titulo = QgsLayoutItemLabel(layout)
titulo.setText('[% "nome_uc" %]')                            # changes on every page
titulo.setFont(QFont("DejaVu Sans", 16, QFont.Weight.Bold))
colocar(titulo, 8, 6, 280, 12)

legenda = QgsLayoutItemLegend(layout)
legenda.setLinkedMap(mapa)
legenda.setTitle("Legend")
colocar(legenda, 214, 22)

norte = QgsLayoutItemPicture(layout)
norte.setPicturePath(":/images/north_arrows/layout_default_north_arrow.svg")
colocar(norte, 270, 138, 15, 15)
norte.setLinkedMap(mapa)

escala = QgsLayoutItemScaleBar(layout)
escala.setLinkedMap(mapa)
escala.setStyle("Single Box")
escala.setUnits(QgsUnitTypes.DistanceKilometers)
escala.setUnitLabel("km")
escala.setNumberOfSegments(2)
escala.setNumberOfSegmentsLeft(0)
escala.setUnitsPerSegment(20)
colocar(escala, 214, 165)

fonte = QgsLayoutItemLabel(layout)
fonte.setText("DETER alerts since 2026-08-01.\nSources: INPE/TerraBrasilis, MMA (CNUC).\n"
              "SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic (EPSG:5880).")
colocar(fonte, 214, 182, 80, 20)

# 3. Atlas: one page per protected area, map centered on it with a 10% margin
atlas = layout.atlas()
atlas.setCoverageLayer(ucs)
atlas.setEnabled(True)
atlas.setFilenameExpression("'mapa_' || \"cnuc\"")
mapa.setAtlasDriven(True)
mapa.setAtlasScalingMode(QgsLayoutItemMap.Auto)
mapa.setAtlasMargin(0.10)

# 4. One PNG image per protected area
config = QgsLayoutExporter.ImageExportSettings()
config.dpi = 150
config.generateWorldFile = False
config.exportMetadata = False
resultado, erro = QgsLayoutExporter.exportToImage(atlas, PASTA + "mapa.png", "png", config)
print("export:", "ok" if resultado == QgsLayoutExporter.Success else erro)
print(sorted(os.listdir(PASTA)))
```

The two tricks that make the atlas look hand-made are in the rule-based style:

- `@atlas_featureid = $id` highlights **the page's protected area** and leaves the neighbors in grey;
- `"cnuc" = attribute(@atlas_feature, 'cnuc')` shows **only the surroundings** of the page's protected
  area.

## PostGIS

PostGIS **does not draw maps**, but it can deliver ready-made layers to QGIS or ArcGIS Pro. A view with
each protected area's recent alerts keeps the map project light and always up to date:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW artigos.mapa_alertas_recentes AS
SELECT d.gid, d.classname, d.view_date, z.cnuc, z.nome_uc, z.local, z.geom
FROM artigos.deter_interior_entorno z
JOIN artigos.deter d USING (gid)
WHERE d.view_date >= current_date - 90;
```

In QGIS, connect to the database (**Browser → PostgreSQL → New Connection**), drag the view onto the map
and use the atlas from the QGIS tab. Every time the database is updated, the atlas comes out with the new
data.

## Python

No GIS program at all: a loop that draws and saves one PNG per protected area.

```python
import os
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

G = "dados/artigos.gpkg"
os.makedirs("dados/mapas_py", exist_ok=True)
ucs = gpd.read_file(G, layer="ucs").query("regiao == 'Amazonia'").to_crs(5880)
entorno = gpd.read_file(G, layer="ucs_entorno").to_crs(5880)
alertas = gpd.read_file(G, layer="deter").to_crs(5880)
alertas = alertas[alertas["view_date"].astype(str) >= "2026-08-01"]

CORES = {"DESMATAMENTO_CR": ("#D55E00", "Deforestation (clear-cut)"),
         "MINERACAO": ("#CC79A7", "Mining"), "DEGRADACAO": ("#E69F00", "Degradation"),
         "CICATRIZ_DE_QUEIMADA": ("#56B4E9", "Burn scar")}
alertas["cor"] = alertas["classname"].map(lambda c: CORES.get(c, ("#787878", ""))[0])

for _, uc in ucs.iterrows():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11.7, 8.3))                    # landscape A4
    xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = uc.geometry.bounds
    m = 0.10 * max(xmax - xmin, ymax - ymin)                       # 10% margin
    ax.set_xlim(xmin - m, xmax + m)
    ax.set_ylim(ymin - m, ymax + m)

    ucs.plot(ax=ax, color="#f2f2f2", edgecolor="#969696", linewidth=0.4)
    entorno[entorno["cnuc"] == uc["cnuc"]].plot(ax=ax, color="#F0E442", alpha=0.55)
    ucs[ucs["cnuc"] == uc["cnuc"]].plot(ax=ax, color="#e5ecdc", edgecolor="black", linewidth=1.2)
    alertas.plot(ax=ax, color=alertas["cor"], linewidth=0)

    # 20 km scale bar, north arrow, legend, title and source
    x0, y0 = ax.get_xlim()[0] + m * 0.4, ax.get_ylim()[0] + m * 0.4
    ax.plot([x0, x0 + 20_000], [y0, y0], color="black", linewidth=3)
    ax.text(x0 + 10_000, y0 + m * 0.12, "20 km", ha="center", fontsize=9)
    ax.annotate("N", xy=(0.95, 0.95), xytext=(0.95, 0.86), xycoords="axes fraction",
                ha="center", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold",
                arrowprops=dict(facecolor="black", width=4, headwidth=12))
    itens = [Patch(facecolor="#e5ecdc", edgecolor="black", label="Mapped protected area"),
             Patch(facecolor="#F0E442", alpha=0.55, label="3 km surroundings")]
    itens += [Patch(color=cor, label=rotulo) for cor, rotulo in CORES.values()]
    ax.legend(handles=itens, loc="upper left", fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9)
    ax.set_title(uc["nome_uc"], fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", loc="left")
    ax.set_axis_off()
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "DETER alerts since 2026-08-01. Sources: INPE/TerraBrasilis, "
             "MMA (CNUC). SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic (EPSG:5880).", fontsize=8)
    fig.savefig(f"dados/mapas_py/mapa_{uc['cnuc']}.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    print("Map of", uc["nome_uc"], "exported")
```

:::

## Checking the result

The QGIS Atlas and the Python loop produced the **7 maps** of the study area, one per protected area,
in a few seconds. The ArcMap and ArcGIS Pro versions follow the same logic, but were not tested here
(they need a license).

## Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning}
## Map in degrees, wrong scale
A map in geographic SIRGAS 2000 (degrees) has a distorted scale bar, and the protected areas look
"squashed" vertically. Put the **map frame** in a projection in meters (here, EPSG:5880), even if the
data stay in degrees.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Atlas that stretches the map frame (QGIS, from code)
When building the layout in Python, if the map starts without an extent, the first atlas page **changes
the size of the frame** and it runs off the page. Give the map an initial extent (`zoomToExtent`) before
turning on the atlas, as in the code above.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## File names
Use the protected area code (`mapa_0000.00.0267.png`), not the name. Accents, spaces and slashes in file
names break scripts and links, especially between Windows and Linux.
:::
